title: Parameter estimation of eccentric massive black hole binaries with LISA and its cosmological implications
summary: Future space-based gravitational wave (GW) observatories such as LISA will detect massive black hole binaries (MBHBs), which are expected to be accompanied by electromagnetic counterparts, thereby providing bright standard sirens for cosmology. The orbital eccentricity of MBHBs can significantly improve the parameter estimation of GWs because the multiple harmonics induced by eccentricity provide additional information and help break down the degeneracies among waveform parameters. In this paper, we use the EccentricFD waveform and construct 5-year GW event catalogs for LISA under three population models (popIII, Q3d and Q3nod). For the three models, we find that an initial eccentricity of $e_0=0.4$ at $10^{-4}$ Hz yields improvements in sky localization and distance inference by a factor of $\mathcal{O}(10)$ in the best cases. As a consequence, the average number of bright sirens increases substantially: from 8 to 11 (PopIII), 6 to 12 (Q3d) and 13 to 24 (Q3nod). This increase in event number, together with enhanced localization and distance inference, leads to tighter cosmological constraints. In the $Λ$CDM model, for instance, the relative uncertainty on $H_0$ is reduced from $8.17\%$ to $4.35\%$ for the Q3d model, corresponding to an improvement of approximately $47\%$. We also investigate the improvement in constraints on the dark energy equation of state and modified GW propagation when combining bright sirens with the latest cosmic microwave background data. These results demonstrate that eccentricity is a remarkably significant feature in GW detection and parameter estimation, enabling more accurate measurements of the Universe with future space-based observatories.

AI.tldr: This paper examines the impact of orbital eccentricity in massive black hole binary detections by future space-based gravitational wave observatories, finding significant improvements in parameter estimation and cosmological constraints.
AI.motivation: To explore how the orbital eccentricity of massive black hole binaries enhances gravitational wave parameter estimation and leads to improved cosmological measurements.
AI.method: Utilizing the EccentricFD waveform, the authors construct 5-year gravitational wave event catalogs for LISA based on three different population models, analyzing the effects of initial eccentricity on sky localization and distance measurements.
AI.result: Initial eccentricity of $e_0=0.4$ showed improvements in sky localization and distance inference by factors of $	ext{O}(10)$, increasing the number of observable bright sirens significantly and leading to tighter cosmological constraints.
AI.conclusion: Eccentricity enhances gravitational wave detection and parameter estimation, providing more accurate cosmological measurements for future space-based observatories.

title: SNAPPY CubeSat Control Script Generation and Data File Processing
comment: Page Count: 11, Figure Count: 6, Table Count: 3; This is a pre-print article intended to be submitted for Nuclear Instruments and Methods A
summary: This is a document discussing the creation and usage of a server system dedicated to retrieving, processing, and storing data generated from the Solar Neutrino and Astro-Particle PhYsics (SNAPPY) CubeSat by the nuSOL (Neutrino Solar Orbiting Laboratory) Project. On a traditional desktop computer with CERN's ROOT and PostgreSQL software installed, and with a file system on two mirrored drives, it is possible to automatically process and organize incoming data, along with keeping a database to record each incoming file along with a command record. In addition to this, an application was created to provide a Graphical User Interface to assist with creating commands to communicate with the CubeSat. With that said, there are still plenty of plans to improve the software, mainly providing an automatic emailing system to notify team members when they are not around the server.

AI.motivation: To efficiently manage and process data generated by the SNAPPY CubeSat within the nuSOL Project, improving accessibility and automation.
AI.method: Developed a server system utilizing CERN's ROOT and PostgreSQL on a desktop computer, featuring a mirrored file system and a GUI for command creation.
AI.result: Successfully automated the processing and organization of incoming data, with a database tracking files and commands.

title: A Fast Generative Framework for High-dimensional Posterior Sampling: Application to CMB Delensing
comment: 12 pages, 4 figures. ML4Astro 2025 workshop paper on fast generative posterior sampling with application to CMB delensing
summary: We introduce a deep generative framework for high-dimensional Bayesian inference that enables efficient posterior sampling. As telescopes and simulations rapidly expand the volume and resolution of astrophysical data, fast simulation-based inference methods are increasingly needed to extract scientific insights. While diffusion-based approaches offer high-quality generative capabilities, they are hindered by slow sampling speeds. Our method performs posterior sampling an order of magnitude faster than a diffusion baseline. Applied to the problem of CMB delensing, it successfully recovers the unlensed CMB power spectrum from simulated observations. The model also remains robust to shifts in cosmological parameters, demonstrating its potential for out-of-distribution generalization and application to observational cosmological data.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a fast deep generative framework for Bayesian inference in high-dimensional astrophysical data, significantly improving sampling speeds compared to existing methods.
AI.motivation: Increasing complexity of astrophysical data necessitates rapid simulation-based inference methods for effective scientific analysis.
AI.method: A deep generative framework that leverages innovative techniques to enhance posterior sampling speed.
AI.result: Achieves posterior sampling an order of magnitude faster than a diffusion-based method and accurately recovers the CMB power spectrum from simulated observations.
AI.conclusion: The model is robust to changes in cosmological parameters and shows promise for broader applications in observational cosmology.

title: Experiments towards a neutron target for measurements in inverse kinematics
summary: Neutron-induced reactions play an important role in fundamental nuclear physics, nuclear astrophysics, and applications. In the case of reactions on rare isotopes, there are limited options for direct experimental measurements. The Neutron Target Demonstrator project at Los Alamos National Laboratory seeks to test the feasibility of moderating spallation neutrons within a 1~m$^3$ graphite cube to create a standing neutron target for neutron-induced reaction measurements in inverse kinematics. This paper presents the results of experimental neutron flux distribution tests using neutron sources (ranging from 1~keV to 50~MeV) created by accelerators at the University of Notre Dame and Texas A\&M University. Measurements were made with both the full graphite cube as well as a ''half cube'' setup in which half of the graphite cube was removed. The measured distributions agree with simulated distributions in the case of the full cube moderator, although there remain discrepancies in certain cases for the half cube moderator. The results shown here will provide useful information for an upcoming experimental campaign to test the neutron target proof-of-principle.

AI.tldr: This paper discusses the Neutron Target Demonstrator project, which tests a neutron moderation technique using a graphite cube for measuring neutron-induced reactions.
AI.motivation: Understanding neutron-induced reactions is crucial in nuclear physics and astrophysics, especially for rare isotopes where experimental options are limited.
AI.method: Experimental tests of neutron flux distribution were conducted using neutron sources from accelerators, comparing a full graphite cube and a modified half cube setup.
AI.result: Results showed that the neutron distributions from the full cube aligned with simulations, while discrepancies were noted in the half cube setup.
AI.conclusion: These findings are valuable for planning future experiments to validate the neutron target concept.

title: Coexistence of Chromatic Flares and an Achromatic QPO in the Gamma-ray Blazar PG 1553+113
comment: 4 pages, 2 figures, 1 table; Accepted by A&A Letters
summary: The physical origin of quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in blazars remains debated, with geometric and plasma-driven scenarios as the main competing interpretations. Discriminating between them requires probing variability beyond flux periodicity. We study the spectral evolution of the BL Lac object PG 1553+113 over its 2.2-year gamma-ray QPO cycle to constrain the mechanism driving the oscillation. In particular, we test whether the variability is chromatic (coupled to spectral changes) or achromatic (independent of spectral shape), allowing us to distinguish between plasma-driven and geometric scenarios. We analyze 17 years of Fermi-LAT data (2008-2025) with 30-day binning. To mitigate red-noise effects, we apply Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA) to remove slow baseline trends and use a Block Bootstrap approach to quantify correlations between photon flux and photon index while preserving temporal dependence. We find a robust softer-when-brighter chromatic trend, atypical for high-synchrotron-peaked blazars such as PG 1553+113 and which, based on our analysis, physically corresponds to softer-when-flaring episodes, that persists after detrending and accounting for temporal autocorrelation. In contrast, no significant correlation is detected between the photon index and the QPO phase, indicating that the periodic modulation is effectively achromatic. The coexistence of plasma-driven chromatic flares and an achromatic QPO disfavors scenarios in which the periodicity arises from intrinsic jet processes. Instead, the results support a geometric origin for the QPO modulation, such as jet precession, where Doppler-factor variations modulate the flux without altering the intrinsic particle energy distribution.

AI.tldr: The study analyzes the spectral evolution of the blazar PG 1553+113 over a 2.2-year gamma-ray QPO cycle to distinguish between potential geometric and plasma-driven interpretations of quasi-periodic oscillations.
AI.motivation: To resolve the ongoing debate regarding the physical origin of QPOs in blazars by examining variability beyond just flux periodicity.
AI.method: The study employs 17 years of Fermi-LAT data with a 30-day binning and uses Singular Spectrum Analysis alongside a Block Bootstrap approach to analyze correlations between photon flux and photon index.
AI.result: The analysis reveals a chromatic trend of 'softer-when-brighter' during flare episodes, while no correlation is found between the photon index and QPO phase, indicating an achromatic nature of QPO.
AI.conclusion: The findings suggest a geometric origin for QPO modulation, such as jet precession, rather than scenarios based on intrinsic jet processes.

title: Air shower development through the time dependence of its induced electric field
summary: Ultra-high energy cosmic rays impinge on the atmosphere and induce air shower cascades, in which huge numbers of particles are produced. By traveling through the Earth's atmosphere and magnetic field, these particles create a noticeable effect on the electric field at the surface. In this article, we demonstrate that parameters of the shower longitudinal development can be inferred from mapping the time dependence of the observed electric field to the emitted electric field as a function of slant depth along the shower axis.

AI.tldr: The paper discusses how electric field variations caused by ultra-high energy cosmic rays can be used to infer parameters of air shower development.
AI.motivation: To explore the connection between electric field effects from cosmic ray-induced air showers and their longitudinal development parameters.
AI.method: The study involves mapping observed electric field time dependence to emitted electric fields over slant depth along the shower axis.
AI.result: The findings indicate that specific parameters of the shower's longitudinal development can be deduced from this mapping technique.
AI.conclusion: This approach enhances the understanding of cosmic ray air showers through electric field analysis.

title: Covariant canonical-spinor amplitudes for partial wave analysis
summary: We propose a covariant orbital-spin ($LS$) decomposed amplitude for the partial wave analysis using the massive spinor-helicity formalism. First we review the traditional-$LS$ method in the little group space and the Zemach tensor method in the double cover of the $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ space. To recover the $\mathrm{SO}(3,1)$ Lorentz covariance, several Lorentz covariant $LS$ tensors have been constructed in several different methods: covariant tensor, covariant projection tensor in pure-spin and general-spin schemes, but performing a intrinsic separation between $LS$ coupling while maintaining covariance is not obvious. We utilize the massive canonical-spinor variables to determine general three-point amplitudes, in which the spin-orbital decomposition is realized in single little group space by projecting little group indices of each particles into one, while the Lorentz covariance is ensured by the spinor form naturally. This covariant spinor method allows direct evaluation in any frame and a streamlined treatment of cascade decays within a single frame without additional alignment rotations in non-covariant treatment. As a benchmark, we implement the method in TF-PWA and analyze $Λ_c^+\toΛπ^+π^0$, finding consistent fit results across the helicity, traditional-$LS$, and canonical-spinor amplitudes. This validates the canonical-spinor amplitude as a practical tool for modern partial wave analyses of complex decay chains.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a covariant orbital-spin decomposed amplitude method for analyzing particle decay processes, enhancing Lorentz covariance in partial wave analyses (PWA).
AI.motivation: To improve the accuracy of partial wave analysis by ensuring Lorentz covariance in spin-orbital decompositions essential for massive particle decays.
AI.method: The method utilizes massive canonical-spinor variables to construct covariant LS tensors, allowing for a natural treatment of particle spins while preserving Lorentz covariance, specifically for analyzing three-point amplitudes.
AI.result: Implementation of the method on the decay process $Λ_c^+\toΛπ^+π^0$ shows results consistent among helicity, traditional-LS, and canonical-spinor amplitudes.
AI.conclusion: The proposed canonical-spinor amplitude framework is validated and demonstrates effectiveness for modern PWA of complex decay chains.

title: Unified Probe of Quantum Chaos and Ergodicity from Hamiltonian Learning
summary: Developing measures of quantum ergodicity and chaos stands as a foundational task in the study of quantum many-body systems. In this work, we propose metrics for these effects based on Hamiltonian learning that unify multiple advantages of existing metrics. In particular, we show how ergodicity and chaos improve the robustness of Hamiltonian learning to small errors and furthermore demonstrate that this robustness can be used as a metric for such phenomena. We analytically and numerically show that our metrics not only distinguish between integrable and ergodic regimes in various spin chains but also quantify chaos and ergodicity, allowing us to locate regions of parameter space displaying maximal ergodicity and maximal sensitivity to local perturbations. Our approach not only provides conceptual ways to study quantum chaos and ergodicity but also presents viable experimental methods for quantum simulators.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes new metrics for quantum ergodicity and chaos based on Hamiltonian learning, showing their application in distinguishing dynamical regimes and quantifying phenomena, thus offering tools for experimental studies in quantum simulators.
AI.motivation: To advance the understanding of quantum ergodicity and chaos within quantum many-body systems by developing unified measures that leverage Hamiltonian learning.
AI.method: The authors introduce metrics derived from Hamiltonian learning to analyze ergodicity and chaos, demonstrating their effectiveness through both analytical and numerical evaluations across different spin chains.
AI.result: The metrics successfully differentiate between integrable and ergodic regimes, quantify chaos and ergodicity, and identify regions with maximal ergodicity and sensitivity to perturbations.
AI.conclusion: This work provides both a conceptual framework and practical methods for exploring quantum chaos and ergodicity, with clear applications in quantum simulation experiments.

title: PulSKASim: A Pulsar Simulator for SKA-Scale Interferometric Observations
comment: Accepted by Astronomical Data Analysis Software and Systems (ADASS) XXXV 2025
summary: Accurate simulation of pulsar flux variability is critical for testing Square Kilometre Array (SKA) interferometric pipelines. However, most existing simulators neglect the effects of integration time and related observational parameters, limiting their realism and utility for interferometric end-to-end testing. To address these shortcomings, we develop a Pulsar Simulator for SKA-scale interferometric observations (PulSKASim), which models pulsar flux evolution across pulsar period, maximum flux, duty cycle, and noise, accounting for integration time, sampling, and observation duration, and naturally models flux smoothing that arises from finite integration within each dump time. PulSKASim generates synthetic measurement sets using functions in simulators for radio interferometers, such as OSKAR and Pyuvsim, where each snapshot contains pulsars with controlled flux levels, enabling realistic per-time-slot experiments. This simulator allows for detailed assessment of calibration, imaging, and detection pipelines under realistic SKA-like conditions, bridging pulsar variability modelling with interferometric simulation in a way not achievable by existing tools.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces PulSKASim, a pulsar simulator that accurately models flux variability for SKA interferometric observations, addressing limitations in existing simulators.
AI.motivation: To enhance the realism and utility of pulsar flux models for SKA testing, overcoming the neglect of integration time and observational parameters in current simulators.
AI.method: PulSKASim simulates pulsar flux evolution, incorporating parameters like period, duty cycle, and noise, while accounting for integration time and flux smoothing due to finite integration.
AI.result: The simulator generates synthetic measurement sets compatible with existing radio interferometer simulators, enabling realistic experiments.
AI.conclusion: PulSKASim allows for comprehensive testing of calibration, imaging, and detection pipelines in a realistic setting, improving upon current tools.

title: Commissioning and Full Realization of the PLASEN System at BRIF
summary: A PLASEN (Precision LAser Spectroscopy for Exotic Nuclei) system, consisting of a compact radio-frequency quadrupole cooler-buncher (RFQ-cb) and a collinear resonance ionization spectroscopy setup, has now been fully commissioned with radioactive ion beams at the Beijing Radioactive Ion-beam Facility (BRIF). Using both stable and radioactive Rb ion beams from BRIF, we demonstrated that the large beam energy spread observed at BRIF has been successfully handled by employing the RFQ-cb, enabling the delivery of high-quality bunched radioactive ion beams for collinear resonance ionization spectroscopy experiments. Under these conditions, we performed laser spectroscopy of exotic nuclei, achieving high resolution (about 100 MHz spectral linewidth) and high sensitivity (up to 1:200 efficiency). This fully operational PLASEN system will serve as a state-of-the-art experimental platform at BRIF for research in multiple fields such as nuclear, atomic and molecular physics.

AI.tldr: The PLASEN system has been successfully commissioned at BRIF, enabling high-resolution laser spectroscopy of exotic nuclei using bunched radioactive ion beams.
AI.motivation: To enhance the study of exotic nuclei through improved beam quality and precision spectroscopy.
AI.method: Utilizing a compact RFQ-cb for cooling and bunching, followed by a collinear resonance ionization spectroscopy setup.
AI.result: Achieved high-resolution (100 MHz) and sensitivity (1:200 efficiency) in laser spectroscopy of exotic nuclei with radioactive ion beams.
AI.conclusion: The PLASEN system represents a cutting-edge platform for diverse research fields at BRIF.

title: Spectral Hardening Revealed by Geometric De-boosting in the Masked Jet of PKS 2155$-$304
comment: 4 pages, 2 figures; Submitted to A&A Letters
summary: Blazar gamma-ray variability is predominantly stochastic and well described by red-noise processes. However, a subset of sources exhibits quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) on year-long timescales, whose physical origin remains debated. In high-synchrotron-peaked (HSP) blazars, departures from a single power-law gamma-ray spectrum, manifested as high-energy upturns in the GeV band, may probe emission mechanisms and the intrinsic duty cycle. We investigate the link between the 1.7 yr gamma-ray QPO in PKS 2155-304 and an exceptional spectral hardening event identified in the Fermi-LAT HSP blazar population. We analyze 18 years of Fermi-LAT data using 30-day binning, applying Singular Spectrum Analysis to mitigate red-noise effects and a Moving Block Bootstrap approach to quantify the correlation between photon flux and photon index. We find a statistically significant softer-when-brighter chromatic trend, supporting a geometric origin of the flux modulation. The spectral hardening event is phase-locked to the QPO trough, implying that the hardening signature is detectable only when geometrically boosted soft emission is suppressed at the flux minimum. We propose a Geometric Masking scenario in which jet geometry regulates the visibility of acceleration processes. These results favor a two-component jet structure and suggest that spectral hardening during low-flux states, even in non-periodic sources, may reveal jet physics otherwise obscured by relativistic amplification.

AI.tldr: The paper explores the link between gamma-ray quasi-periodic oscillations in PKS 2155-304 and spectral hardening events, suggesting a geometric origin tied to jet structure.
AI.motivation: Understanding the physical origin of quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in blazars and their relationship with spectral changes is crucial for probing emission mechanisms and intrinsic jet dynamics.
AI.method: The authors analyzed 18 years of Fermi-LAT data using 30-day binning and employed Singular Spectrum Analysis to reduce red-noise influence, along with a Moving Block Bootstrap method to assess correlations between photon flux and indices.
AI.result: A significant softer-when-brighter trend was found, indicating a geometric origin for flux variability, with spectral hardening events occurring in correlation with flux minima.
AI.conclusion: The findings support a two-component jet structure and highlight that spectral hardening during low-flux states may reveal hidden aspects of jet dynamics, influenced by relativistic effects.

title: Matter Unification and Lepton Flavour Violation
summary: We explore the idea of quark-lepton unification at low energies. In particular, we discuss the minimal framework for matter unification at the multi-TeV scale, in which neutrino masses are necessarily generated via the inverse seesaw mechanism. To assess the testability of this theory for physics beyond the Standard Model, we analyze current experimental constraints and derive the corresponding lower bound on the symmetry breaking scale. We reexamine the impact of existing limits from lepton number violating meson decays, taking into account the freedom associated with unknown quark-lepton mixing angles. Furthermore, we study the correlation between bounds from meson decays and $μ\to e$ conversion. We demonstrate that the upcoming $μ\to e$ conversion experiment at Fermilab can play a crucial role in probing quark-lepton unification at the multi-TeV scale.

AI.tldr: The paper examines quark-lepton unification at low energies, focusing on a scenario where neutrino masses arise from the inverse seesaw mechanism. It evaluates experimental constraints and derives limits on the symmetry breaking scale, emphasizing the significance of the upcoming Fermilab experiment in testing this theory.
AI.motivation: To investigate the feasibility of quark-lepton unification at low energies and understand neutrino mass generation mechanisms.
AI.method: Analysis of experimental constraints, derivation of lower bounds on the symmetry breaking scale, and examination of lepton number violation and mixing angles.
AI.result: Identified limits from meson decays and established correlation with $μ	o e$ conversion, showing the relevance of these limits for quark-lepton unification.
AI.conclusion: The Fermilab $μ	o e$ conversion experiment is pivotal for testing the proposed multi-TeV scale quark-lepton unification framework.

title: Domain Walls from $Σ(36 \times 3)$, $Δ(54)$ and $Δ(27)$ potentials
summary: We consider the degenerate minima arising from scalar potentials invariant under $Σ(36\times 3)$, or under its subgroups $Δ(54)$ and $Δ(27)$ (with or without imposed CP symmetries), for a triplet of those symmetries. In this framework, we classify the distinct Domain Walls between the degenerate minima and calculate the respective tensions.

AI.tldr: The paper classifies Domain Walls from degenerate minima of scalar potentials invariant under specific symmetry groups, computing their tensions.
AI.motivation: To explore degenerate minima in scalar potentials linked to certain symmetry groups, enhancing understanding of field dynamics.
AI.method: Classification of Domain Walls formulating connections between degenerate minima and analyzing their tensions.
AI.result: Distinct types of Domain Walls were identified, with computed tensions for each type based on their symmetrical properties.
AI.conclusion: The findings provide insights into the dynamics of fields with degenerate minima influenced by symmetry, paving the way for further research.

title: Rethinking quantum smooth entropies: Tight one-shot analysis of quantum privacy amplification
summary: We introduce an improved one-shot characterisation of randomness extraction against quantum side information (privacy amplification), strengthening known one-shot bounds and providing a unified derivation of the tightest known asymptotic constraints. Our main tool is a new class of smooth conditional entropies defined by lifting classical smooth divergences through measurements. For the key case of measured smooth Rényi divergence of order 2, we show that this can be alternatively understood as allowing for smoothing over not only states, but also non-positive Hermitian operators. Building on this, we establish a tightened leftover hash lemma, significantly improving over all known smooth min-entropy bounds on quantum privacy amplification and recovering the sharpest classical achievability results. We extend these methods to decoupling, the coherent analogue of randomness extraction, obtaining a corresponding improved one-shot bound. Relaxing our smooth entropy bounds leads to one-shot achievability results in terms of measured Rényi divergences, which in the asymptotic i.i.d. limit recover the state-of-the-art error exponent of [Dupuis, arXiv:2105.05342]. We show an approximate optimality of our results by giving a matching one-shot converse bound up to additive logarithmic terms. This yields an optimal second-order asymptotic expansion of privacy amplification under trace distance, establishing a significantly tighter one-shot achievability result than previously shown in [Shen et al., arXiv:2202.11590] and proving its optimality for all hash functions.

AI.tldr: This paper improves randomness extraction against quantum side information through a novel class of smooth conditional entropies, establishing tighter bounds and achieving optimal results for privacy amplification.
AI.motivation: To strengthen existing one-shot bounds for randomness extraction and provide a unified approach to tight asymptotic constraints in quantum settings.
AI.method: Introduction of a new class of smooth conditional entropies, particularly using measured smooth Rényi divergence of order 2, and development of an improved leftover hash lemma for quantum privacy amplification.
AI.result: Establishes enhanced bounds for privacy amplification and decoupling, and shows achievement of optimal error exponents, surpassing previous results.
AI.conclusion: Results indicate significant advancements in one-shot achievability for randomness extraction, optimality for hash functions, and improvements over previous research benchmarks.

title: AstroInspect: a web-based system to organize, assess, and visually inspect astronomical objects
comment: 20 pages, 7 figures, 1 table, accepted in AJ
summary: The rapid growth of imaging and spectroscopic surveys has intensified the need for efficient tools that support visual inspection, a practice that remains essential for tasks such as classification, catalog refinement, and validation of automated methods. Existing solutions, however, often require the use of multiple platforms and complex workflows to integrate heterogeneous data. To address this challenge, we present the first release of the AstroInspect (https://astroinspect.github.io), a web-based system which ensures seamless access to several astronomical resources. The system provides an intuitive graphical user interface (GUI) through which users can upload catalogs of objects defined by celestial coordinates. AstroInspect automatically enriches these catalogs with complementary information, including imaging, spectroscopic, and photometric data retrieved in real time from surveys such as the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS), the Legacy Surveys (LS), and the Southern Photometric Local Universe Survey (S-PLUS). As an example of its scientific utility, we used AstroInspect to identify H$α$ emission-line galaxies within a 7 deg radius in the direction of the Hydra I cluster (also known as Abell 1060) by visual inspection. Using a candidate set of 981 galaxies selected from S-PLUS photometric data, we produced a catalog of 80 galaxies with confirmed H$α$ emission. These results highlight the potential of AstroInspect to support efficient visual inspection workflows.

AI.tldr: AstroInspect is a web-based tool designed to facilitate the visual inspection of astronomical data by integrating various resources in an intuitive interface.
AI.motivation: The increase in astronomical surveys necessitates efficient tools for visual inspections crucial for classification and validation tasks.
AI.method: AstroInspect allows users to upload celestial object catalogs and enriches them with imaging, spectroscopic, and photometric data from major telescopes in real time.
AI.result: Using AstroInspect, 80 H$α$ emission-line galaxies were confirmed from a candidate set of 981 galaxies identified within a specific region of the Hydra I cluster.
AI.conclusion: AstroInspect demonstrates significant potential in enhancing efficiency in visual inspection workflows for astronomical research.

title: Fast array-based particle coincidence detection in a TimePix3-based velocity map imaging instrument
summary: With the development of high repetition rate laser sources and advanced multi-particle correlation analyses such as covariance mapping, particle detection techniques such as velocity map imaging (VMI) are poised to offer unprecedented views into molecular phenomena. Taking full advantage of the high count rates in these experiments requires the development of detectors with sufficient spatial and temporal resolution that can process data in real time. The TimePix3 camera (TPX3CAM) is an event-based pixel detector capable of spatio-temporally localizing many simultaneous particle hits in an efficient manner. While the sparse nature of the data stream allows for compact representation of particle hits, it also presents algorithmic and computational challenges for clustering individual pixels into hits. Here we present the theory and application of a rapid data processing and centroiding algorithm for ion and electron hits collected in a VMI instrument. The array-based computations that comprise the algorithm take full advantage of the data sparsity of the TimePix3 data stream and localize particle hits on the microchannel plate (MCP) to better than a single pixel on the pixel detector. Centroiding can be parallelized on a commercially available graphics processing unit (GPU) for additional speed. Using these innovations, data processing occurs about 25 times faster than data acquisition, for a 1 kHz repetition rate instrument and tens of particles per shot. In addition to its speed, the TPX3CAM detector outperforms state-of-the-art delay line anode detectors at discriminating multiple simultaneous hits, enabling high-fidelity coincidence and covariance studies in the near future.

AI.tldr: Development of high-speed detectors like the TimePix3 camera enhances data processing for molecular studies, achieving significant speed improvements and accuracy in particle hit localization.
AI.motivation: To leverage advances in laser technology and correlation analyses for detailed insights into molecular phenomena through improved detection methods.
AI.method: The study introduces a rapid data processing and centroiding algorithm tailored for event-based pixel detection in VMI instruments, optimized for the TimePix3 camera's data stream and utilizing GPU acceleration.
AI.result: Achieved data processing speeds approximately 25 times faster than acquisition rates, with improved localization precision of particle hits beyond single pixel resolution, demonstrating superior performance compared to existing detection technologies.
AI.conclusion: The TimePix3 camera, equipped with the new processing algorithm, enables high-fidelity coincidence and covariance studies in molecular phenomena, significantly enhancing experimental capabilities.

title: Geometric masking in AGN jets and its implications for unification and blazar physics
summary: We explore the implications of the recently proposed Geometric Masking scenario for the Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) Unification Scheme, the blazar sequence, and broader blazar phenomenology, and assess its consistency with recent observations. Phase-resolved analysis of PKS 2155$-$304 shows that extreme GeV spectral hardening events are locked to the trough of its $\sim 1.7$ yr quasi-periodic oscillation, indicating that high-flux states are dominated by a soft, geometrically amplified envelope that outshines an underlying hard core. Independent support comes from the detection of TeV emission in the FSRQs S5 1027+74 and 3C 273 when integrating over low-flux states, revealing hard spectra inconsistent with a purely cooling-dominated interpretation. We argue that Doppler boosting preferentially enhances the soft component when the jet is closely aligned, creating a visibility bias that extends the AGN Unification Scheme and introduces a geometric modulation layer within the blazar sequence. In this framework, low-flux states correspond to windows of geometric transparency rather than intrinsic quiescence, and misaligned systems act as permanently unmasked laboratories of particle acceleration. The scenario implies that the duty cycle of extreme acceleration in AGN jets is substantially higher than inferred from flux-selected observations.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates the Geometric Masking scenario's impact on AGN unification, linking observations of spectral behavior in specific blazars to enhanced understanding of jet dynamics and particle acceleration.
AI.motivation: To examine how Geometric Masking influences AGN unification and blazar behavior, aligning with recent observational data.
AI.method: Phase-resolved analysis of PKS 2155$-$304 and TeV emission observations from FSRQs to assess spectral characteristics and Doppler effects in high and low-flux states.
AI.result: The analysis reveals that high-flux states exhibit a soft envelope dominating over a hard core, and TeV observations indicate enhanced soft spectra during aligned jet conditions.
AI.conclusion: The study suggests that low-flux states reflect geometric transparency rather than inactivity, indicating a higher than previously estimated frequency of extreme particle acceleration in AGN jets.

title: A baryon-calibrated unified quark-diquark effective mass formalism for heavy multiquarks
summary: We present a unified framework for heavy tetraquark and pentaquark systems within the quark-diquark effective mass formalism, extending its baryon-calibrated construction to multiquark states without introducing sector-dependent parameters. Intra-diquark color-spin correlations are encoded in effective diquark masses fixed from baryon spectroscopy, while the inter-cluster chromomagnetic scale, independently determined from vector-pseudoscalar meson splittings, is propagated unchanged to exotic configurations, ensuring residual one-gluon exchange dynamics only between composite color sources. Within this framework, we compute the complete spectra for both $\bar{\mathbf{3}}_c\otimes\mathbf{3}_c$ and $\mathbf{6}_c\otimes\bar{\mathbf{6}}_c$ configurations in tetraquarks, whereas the pentaquark analysis focuses on the dominant $\bar{\mathbf{3}}_c\otimes\bar{\mathbf{3}}_c\otimes\bar{\mathbf{3}}_c$ clustering. Heavy-quark spin symmetry and flavor-symmetry breaking across light, charm, and bottom sectors emerge naturally through the explicit $1/(m_{D_1}m_{D_2})$ scaling of the calibrated couplings. The resulting spectra exhibit a coherent dynamical hierarchy spanning baryons and multiquark states. Established exotic candidates are reproduced within hadronic uncertainties, while the unified calibration enables quantitative predictive control across flavor sectors. The framework thus provides a parameter-economical, systematically constrained baseline with unified dynamical consistency for heavy multiquark spectroscopy.

AI.tldr: A unified framework for analyzing heavy tetraquark and pentaquark systems is developed, leveraging quark-diquark effective mass formalism and baryon-calibrated parameters for predictive control in multiquark spectroscopy.
AI.motivation: To create a standardized method for studying heavy tetraquarks and pentaquarks without introducing additional parameters, ensuring consistency across different configurations and incorporating established theoretical frameworks.
AI.method: Incorporates baryon-calibrated effective diquark masses and an independently determined chromomagnetic scale to compute the spectra for various multiquark configurations, focusing on tetraquarks and pentaquarks.
AI.result: The analysis yields coherent spectra for tetraquarks and pentaquarks consistent with hadronic uncertainties, effectively reproducing established exotic candidates and capturing scaling behavior across flavor sectors.
AI.conclusion: This framework offers a systematic, parameter-light baseline for exploring heavy multiquark spectroscopy, highlighting its dynamical consistency and predictive capability across different flavor configurations.

title: Momentum fraction and hard scale dependence of double parton scattering in heavy-ion collisions
summary: In a previous work, we studied the momentum fraction and hard--scale dependence of double parton scattering (DPS) in proton--proton collisions and the resulting dependence of the effective cross section on the final--state observables. In this paper, we extend those results to heavy--ion ($pA$ and $AA$) collisions, accounting for nuclear effects in the relevant kinematic region, namely shadowing and antishadowing. In addition to modifying the longitudinal parton distributions, these effects also alter the transverse parton distribution of the nucleus, for which we propose a simple model. We further hypothesize that partons inside a bound nucleon are more widely separated than in a free proton. We compute the effective cross section for the available $p$Pb data, obtaining reasonable agreement, and provide predictions for future measurements at the LHC. The observed dependence of our predictions on the final state indicates that DPS in heavy--ion collisions can be used to probe the transverse profile of the free proton and the bound nucleon, primarily in $pA$ collisions, as well as the transverse structure of the nucleus, mainly in $AA$ collisions.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the study of double parton scattering (DPS) from proton-proton to heavy-ion collisions, introducing a model to account for nuclear effects.
AI.motivation: To analyze the impact of nuclear effects on double parton scattering in heavy-ion collisions and their implications for effective cross sections derived from final-state observables.
AI.method: The authors account for shadowing and antishadowing in longitudinal and transverse parton distributions and develop a model for the transverse parton distribution of the nucleus.
AI.result: The study computes effective cross sections for existing $p$Pb data with reasonable agreement and predicts outcomes for future LHC measurements.
AI.conclusion: DPS in heavy-ion collisions can reveal insights into the transverse structure of free and bound nucleons, providing valuable data for both $pA$ and $AA$ collision analyses.

title: Quantum State Certification via Effective Parent Hamiltonians from Local Measurement Data
summary: The preparation and certification of quantum states is a fundamental challenge across quantum information technology. We introduce a tomography-free state certification method that lower-bounds the fidelity by estimating expectation values of engineered parent-Hamiltonian terms from local measurement data. We apply this framework to construct a parent Hamiltonian that enables certification and variational optimization across the Dicke-state family, which includes the single-excitation $W_n$ state. We experimentally validate the framework on IBM quantum hardware, certifying genuine multipartite entanglement for $W_n$ states up to six qubits and establishing positive lower bounds on the state fidelity up to thirteen qubits. For Dicke states with two- and three-excitations, we certify genuine multipartite entanglement up to seven qubits. Within this stringent certification framework, these results constitute among the largest witness-certified demonstrations of such states on a programmable quantum processor.

AI.tldr: A new method for certifying quantum states is introduced that uses local measurements to estimate fidelity without full tomography, successfully applied to Dicke states on IBM quantum hardware.
AI.motivation: Quantum state preparation and certification is crucial for developments in quantum information technology.
AI.method: A tomography-free approach that estimates the fidelity of quantum states by evaluating expectation values of parent-Hamiltonian terms from local measurements.
AI.result: The method enables certification of multipartite entanglement for Dicke states, validated experimentally on quantum hardware, achieving certification for states up to six qubits and fidelity assessment up to thirteen qubits.
AI.conclusion: This framework represents a significant advancement in the certification of multipartite entangled states on quantum processors, demonstrating large-scale entanglement with high fidelity guarantees.

title: A New Method for Identifying Contaminating Sources and Locating Target Sources through the Cross-Arm Features of Micro Pore Optics
summary: The Pathfinder of the Type-A satellites in the Chasing All Transients Constellation Hunters (CATCH) space mission is equipped with Micro-Pore Optics (MPOs) and four single-pixel Silicon Drift Detectors (SDDs). Due to the lack of position resolution in an individual SDD, we propose a new method based on the cross-arms in the point spread function (PSF) of MPOs to enhance the satellite's capability in identifying contaminating sources and locating target sources. By placing one detector on each of the horizontal and vertical cross-arms on the focal plane, we can use the changes in the relative counts on the cross-arms detectors to deduce the location of the source. Simulated observations demonstrate that, for a target source with a flux of 1 Crab and an exposure time of 200 s, the cross-arms detectors can identify contaminating source with the same flux level at an off-axis angle larger than 8', and improve positioning accuracy to 6'. Furthermore, we extend the simulation study to CATCH Type-A, which plans to use an SDD array. In situations where sources exhibit the same flux of 1 Crab and the exposure time is merely 1 s, a 16x16 SDD array is capable of identifying contaminating source with an off-axis angle greater than 2.4' and can achieve a positioning precision of 1.8'.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a method to enhance source localization for the CATCH mission using cross-arms in the PSF of MPOs, improving positioning accuracy with SDDs.
AI.motivation: To enhance the identification and localization of sources in space missions, particularly overcoming the limitation of single-pixel SDDs.
AI.method: Utilizing cross-arms in the PSF of MPOs to position detectors strategically, allowing for determination of source locations based on count variations in the detectors.
AI.result: Simulations show improved identification of contaminating sources at specific flux levels and off-axis angles, achieving notable positioning accuracies with both single-pixel and array configurations.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method significantly enhances the capability of satellite systems in accurately localizing astronomical sources, paving the way for advanced observation strategies in the CATCH mission.

title: Improved supernova bounds on CP-even scalars: cooling and decay constraints
summary: Supernovae provide among the most powerful probes of weakly-coupled new particles in the MeV mass range, where laboratory experiments lose sensitivity. In this work, we derive improved supernova constraints on CP-even scalars mixing with the Higgs boson, combining an updated production rate calculation, which improves the cooling bound by more than an order of magnitude, with new decay-based constraints from the galactic 511~keV positron flux and energy deposition in low-energy Type~II-P supernovae. Together, these constraints probe mixing angles as small as $\sinθ\sim 10^{-9}$, more than five orders of magnitude below existing collider bounds. We also extend our analysis to a hadrophilic scalar model, constraining Yukawa couplings down to $y_N \sim 10^{-10}$. Our results demonstrate that the combination of astrophysical and collider probes covers over nine orders of magnitude in coupling for these classes of models, probing a large region of parameter space motivated by dark matter considerations.

AI.tldr: This paper enhances supernova constraints on new scalar particles that mix with the Higgs boson, achieving sensitivity to very small mixing angles and coupling constants.
AI.motivation: To explore the effects of weakly-coupled new particles in the MeV mass range, where traditional laboratory experiments are ineffective, particularly in relation to dark matter theories.
AI.method: The authors improve supernova constraints by recalculating production rates and incorporating new decay constraints from positron flux and energy deposition in Type II-P supernovae.
AI.result: The research demonstrates sensitivity to mixing angles as small as $	ext{sin} 	heta 	hickapprox 10^{-9}$ and Yukawa couplings down to $y_N 	hickapprox 10^{-10}$, surpassing existing collider limits by several orders of magnitude.
AI.conclusion: Astrophysical and collider data together provide a comprehensive probe of scalar particle models, significantly expanding the search parameters in light of dark matter theories.

title: Fundamental Limits on Polarization Entanglement Distribution in Optical Fiber
summary: Characterizing the ultimate rates of entanglement distribution is essential for both foundational research and the practical deployment of quantum technologies. To investigate these limits, we introduce an erasure-Pauli channel model describing the distribution of polarization entanglement in optical fiber. For this channel, we derive bounds on the rates of entanglement distribution and related quantum resources under optimal local operations and two-way classical communication (two-way assisted capacities). This framework allows us to determine the optimal repeaterless performance achievable over realistic optical fibers affected by polarization mode dispersion, thereby providing a rigorous benchmark for long-distance polarization-based quantum communication. Finally, we show that both our model and capacity bounds remain robust under the inclusion of detector dark counts.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a model for erasure-Pauli channels to analyze entanglement distribution in optical fiber and establishes bounds on distribution rates under specific conditions, considering practical limitations like polarization mode dispersion and detector dark counts.
AI.motivation: Understanding entanglement distribution is crucial for advancing quantum technologies and establishing benchmarks for practical applications.
AI.method: The authors present an erasure-Pauli channel model and derive bounds on entanglement distribution rates using optimal local operations and two-way classical communication.
AI.result: The derived bounds provide a benchmark for repeaterless performance in optical fibers impacted by polarization mode dispersion and show resilience against detector dark counts.
AI.conclusion: The study offers a rigorous framework for assessing entanglement distribution in practical quantum communication scenarios, ensuring robust performance predictions in realistic conditions.

title: MWA tied-array processing V: Super-resolved localisation via amplitude-only maximum likelihood direction finding
comment: 10 pages, 5 figures. Accepted for publication in PASA
summary: Interferometric localisation of transients and pulsars via tied-array beam processing is challenging and can be limited by the native spatial resolution achievable by the instrument, especially at low frequencies and for compact interferometers. Knowledge of the telescope primary and tied-array beam patterns allows the exploitation of the beam structures and the relationship to measured quantities, such as signal-to-noise ratio, through radio direction finding techniques. The additional information provides a "super-resolved" localisation (i.e., where the precision is much better than the native spatial resolution) of a source when there are multiple detections in adjacent tied-array beams. We demonstrate this approach using the Murchison Widefield Array (MWA) and its voltage capture and tied-array processing capabilities, with a specific focus on how it benefits the on-going Southern-sky MWA Rapid Two-metre pulsar survey as it starts producing more candidates requiring follow-up. Examples of localisations with previously discovered MWA pulsars which were subsequently localised via imaging with higher spatial resolution interferometers are used to validate the process, along with localisations of a sample of known pulsars to demonstrate the robustness of the method and its uncertainty estimation.

AI.tldr: This paper discusses a method for enhancing the localisation of transients and pulsars using tied-array beam processing, leveraging telescope beam patterns for better accuracy beyond standard resolution.
AI.motivation: To improve the localization of pulsars and transients, especially in low-frequency and compact interferometer settings, where native resolution limits precision.
AI.method: The authors employ knowledge of telescope beam patterns in conjunction with radio direction finding techniques to achieve 'super-resolved' localisation of sources detected by multiple tied-array beams.
AI.result: The approach is demonstrated using the Murchison Widefield Array (MWA), showing enhanced localisation capabilities and validation through examples of known pulsars.
AI.conclusion: This method provides a reliable framework for localizing pulsars more accurately, benefiting ongoing surveys by efficiently processing signals from multiple detections.

title: Sensitivity of a closed dielectric haloscope to axion dark matter
summary: We present a method to determine the sensitivity of a closed dielectric haloscope to axion dark matter. Dielectric haloscopes aim to probe the theoretically well-motivated axion mass range of ~26 $\mathrmμ$eV to ~500 $\mathrmμ$eV by utilizing a stack of dielectric disks and a mirror to enhance the axion-photon conversion within an external magnetic field. Their conversion volume is nearly axion-mass independent, thereby favoring large-scale designs to increase sensitivity. The large volume causes simulations to be computationally expensive and time-consuming. This paper presents a simple model that can be used to determine the sensitivity of the experiment with minimal computational resources. The model is able to describe the electromagnetic response of a closed dielectric haloscope, accounting for realistic geometric imperfections, as well as the noise introduced by the receiver system. It is applied to data taken with a MAgnetized Disk and Mirror Axion Experiment (MADMAX) prototype within the 1.6 T Morpurgo magnet at CERN. This work underpins the first axion dark matter search using a dielectric haloscope and provides the foundation for future dark matter searches with MADMAX.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a method to assess the sensitivity of dielectric haloscopes for axion dark matter detection, demonstrating a resource-efficient model that accommodates geometric imperfections and noise.
AI.motivation: The aim is to explore the axion mass range of ~26 μeV to ~500 μeV, which is theoretically significant for axion dark matter.
AI.method: A simple model is developed to analyze the electromagnetic response of closed dielectric haloscopes, factoring in geometric imperfections and receiver noise.
AI.result: The model effectively determines the sensitivity of the experiment while minimizing computational demands and is validated by applying it to data from the MADMAX prototype at CERN.
AI.conclusion: This work lays the groundwork for future axion dark matter searches using dielectric haloscopes, particularly with MADMAX.

title: 50 Years of SUSY and SUGRA, circa 1974-2024, and Future Prospects
summary: The development in the early seventies of supersymmetry, in the mid-seventies of gauge supersymmetry and supergravity, and in the early eighties of gravity mediated breaking of supersymmetry and of supergravity grand unification have led to remarkable progress in the pursuit of unification of fundamental interactions of particle physics. They have also led to the intertwining of particle physics, cosmology, and strings. Since supersymmetry and supergravity are manifest in the low energy limit of superstring below the Planck scale, experimental test of them are of interest regarding the validity of the superstring itself. For that reason, over the past decades, after the advent of supersymmetry and SUGRA models, there have been sustained experimental searches for supersymmetry at colliders, in precision experiments, and in astrophysical and cosmological data. The SUSY and SUGRA models have also had deep impact on theories related to inflation, dark matter, and dark energy. The purpose of this article is to provide a view from the bridge of these developments over the past fifty years circa 1974-2024.

AI.tldr: This article reviews the historical development and significance of supersymmetry (SUSY) and supergravity (SUGRA) in unifying fundamental interactions in particle physics, and their implications in cosmology and string theory, emphasizing ongoing experimental efforts and their impact on theories of inflation, dark matter, and dark energy.
AI.motivation: To explore the interconnections between supersymmetry, supergravity, and fundamental interactions in particle physics, as well as their implications for cosmology and string theory.
AI.method: The article reviews the historical milestones in the development of SUSY and SUGRA from the 1970s to the present, analyzing their experimental search efforts and contributions to broader theories in physics.
AI.result: The article outlines the positive influence of SUSY and SUGRA on various fields, including inflation, dark matter, and dark energy, alongside ongoing experimental searches that seek to validate these theories.
AI.conclusion: It provides a comprehensive overview of the evolution of these concepts over fifty years, highlighting their foundational role in modern theoretical physics.

title: Markovian quantum master equations are exponentially accurate in the weak coupling regime
comment: 5 pages and 1 figure in main text. 15 pages in supplement
summary: We consider the evolution of open quantum systems coupled to one or more Gaussian environments. We demonstrate that such systems can be described by a Markovian quantum master equation (MQME) up to a correction that decreases exponentially with the inverse system-bath coupling strength. We provide an explicit expression for this MQME, along with rigorous bounds on its residual correction, and numerically benchmark it for an exactly solvable model. The MQME is obtained via a generalized Born-Markov approximation that can be iterated to arbitrary orders in the system-bath coupling; our error bound converges asymptotically to zero with the iteration order. Our results thus demonstrate that the non-Markovian component in the evolution of an open quantum system, while possibly inevitable, can be exponentially suppressed at weak coupling.

AI.tldr: This paper discusses a Markovian quantum master equation (MQME) applicable to open quantum systems in Gaussian environments, showing that non-Markovian effects can be suppressed exponentially with weak coupling.
AI.motivation: To enhance understanding of the behavior of open quantum systems interacting with Gaussian environments and to quantify the effects of non-Markovian dynamics in these systems.
AI.method: The authors derive an MQME using a generalized Born-Markov approximation and present rigorous bounds on the residual correction, supported by numerical benchmarks on a solvable model.
AI.result: An explicit MQME is developed, demonstrating that the non-Markovian effects can diminish exponentially with the inverse system-bath coupling strength, confirmed through rigorous bounds and numerical analysis.
AI.conclusion: The findings indicate that while non-Markovian dynamics are inherent to open quantum systems, their influence can be significantly reduced in cases of weak coupling.

title: Could the interaction of jet and SN ejecta be the cause of X-ray knots observed in a radio galaxy?
summary: We investigate the interaction between relativistic jets and supernova (SN) ejecta as a potential origin of X-ray knots in radio galaxies, employing knot A in M 87 as a test case. By modeling the dynamical evolution of the interaction, we evaluate this scenario based on particle acceleration efficiency and spatial morphology. Our modeling indicates that the ejecta shock expands to only ~ 30 pc, which is inconsistent with the observed spatial scale of knot A (~ 60 pc). In contrast, the jet shock can successfully reproduce the observed scale after approximately 3000 yr, with the ejecta being accelerated to a bulk velocity of β~ 0.43. We fit the multi-wavelength spectral energy distribution (SED) using a one-zone leptonic framework, attributing the X-rays to synchrotron radiation from electrons accelerated up to~1 PeV at the jet shock. The derived magnetic field is approximately 70 uG in the SN ejecta rest frame, which is significantly below the equipartition value. Protons may be accelerated up to ~ EeV, supporting the hypothesis that the jets of radio galaxies (RGs) may be the potential site for ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray (UHECR) acceleration within the framework of the jet-ejecta interaction.

AI.tldr: The study examines the interaction between relativistic jets and supernova ejecta to explain X-ray knots in radio galaxies, concluding that jet shocks are more effective in creating observed features than ejecta shocks.
AI.motivation: To understand the formation of X-ray knots in radio galaxies, specifically using M 87's knot A as a case study.
AI.method: The research models the dynamical interaction between relativistic jets and supernova ejecta, assessing particle acceleration efficiency and spatial morphology.
AI.result: Ejecta shocks expand to ~30 pc, not matching knot A's observed ~60 pc, while jet shocks can match this scale after ~3000 years, with ejecta accelerated to ~0.43c and generating X-rays via synchrotron radiation.
AI.conclusion: The findings suggest that jet-ejecta interactions in radio galaxies can be significant sites for ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray acceleration, although magnetic fields are below equipartition levels.

title: On the robustness of the indirect determination of the width of the detected Higgs boson
summary: The indirect determination of the total width of the detected Higgs boson that is carried out by the experimental collaborations at the LHC relies on the assumption that the coupling modifiers for the on-shell and off-shell couplings are the same. However, physics beyond the Standard Model affecting the on-shell and off-shell regions differently could invalidate this assumption, so that the actual width of the detected Higgs boson could be larger than the bounds obtained under this assumption. Relaxing the assumption and investigating different types of extensions of the Standard Model, we analyse under which conditions a larger total width of the detected Higgs boson is compatible with all experimental and theoretical constraints. For the considered scenarios of scalar extensions with an additional state contributing as a resonance or at the loop level, we find that the indirect bounds obtained by ATLAS and CMS remain valid over large parts of the parameter space, with the exception of parameter regions where the additional particles have relatively small masses. We discuss the potential of experimental searches for new particles to further constrain such scenarios. Based on the existing experimental and theoretical constraints we conclude that relaxing the assumption of equal on-shell and off-shell coupling modifiers that is used in the experimental analyses at the LHC yields an upper bound on the total width of the detected Higgs boson in realistic extensions of the Standard Model that is only weakened by up to a factor of about two compared to the case where this assumption is valid.

AI.tldr: The paper examines how relaxing the assumption that on-shell and off-shell Higgs couplings are identical affects the estimated total width of the Higgs boson, finding that a larger width is possible under certain model extensions.
AI.motivation: To investigate the potential discrepancies in Higgs boson coupling modifiers and their implications on the total width of the Higgs boson, particularly in the context of physics beyond the Standard Model.
AI.method: The analysis involves relaxing the assumption of equal on-shell and off-shell coupling modifiers while exploring various Standard Model extensions, and evaluating their compatibility with existing experimental and theoretical constraints.
AI.result: The study reveals that the indirect bounds by ATLAS and CMS are valid over most of the parameter space, except where additional low-mass particles are considered, suggesting a larger Higgs width could still align with experimental data.
AI.conclusion: The findings indicate that relaxing the coupling modifiers' assumption yields an upper bound on the Higgs boson width that is weakened by at most a factor of two compared to when the assumption holds.

title: The effect of charm quark on the QCD chiral phase diagram
summary: We study the influence of charm quark dynamics on the chiral phase structure of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) using the recently developed miniDSE scheme of the Dyson-Schwinger equations. By calculating the quark propagator in $2+1$ and $2+1+1$ flavor QCD, we quantify the impact of including the charm quark as a dynamical degree of freedom on the QCD phase diagram. Our results show that the charm quark induces a moderate but noticeable shift to lower chemical potential in the location of the critical endpoint (CEP) by approximately 2-3%. The result in this work indicates that the heavy-flavor dynamics can subtly influence the QCD phase structure and should be taken into account in particular for searching the CEP of QCD.

AI.tldr: The study explores how charm quark dynamics affect the chiral phase structure of QCD, revealing a 2-3% shift in the critical endpoint due to charm quark inclusion.
AI.motivation: To understand the effects of charm quark dynamics on the QCD phase diagram and the location of the critical endpoint.
AI.method: Utilized the miniDSE scheme of Dyson-Schwinger equations to calculate the quark propagator in 2+1 and 2+1+1 flavor QCD.
AI.result: Including the charm quark alters the critical endpoint's location, shifting it to lower chemical potential by about 2-3%.
AI.conclusion: Heavy-flavor dynamics, particularly those of the charm quark, significantly impact the QCD phase structure and are crucial for identifying the critical endpoint.

title: Towards Predictive Quantum Algorithmic Performance: Modeling Time-Correlated Noise at Scale
summary: Combining tensor network techniques with quantum autoregressive moving average models, we quantify the effects of time-correlated noise on quantum algorithms and predict their performance at scale. As a paradigmatic test case, we examine the quantum Fourier transformation. Building on our first technical result, which shows how stochastic tensor network calculations capture frequency correlations, our second result is the revelation that infidelity exponents (scaling from diffuse, to superdiffuse) are determined by the spectral features of the noise. This numerical result rigorously quantifies the common belief that the temporal correlation scale is a key predictive feature of noise's deleterious impact on multi-qubit circuits. To highlight prospects for predicting algorithmic performance, our third result quantifies how infidelity scaling exponents -- which are fits determined by training data at moderate scales (40-80 qubits) -- can be used to predict more computationally expensive simulation at larger scales (100-128 qubits). Aside from highlighting the scalability of our methods, this workflow feeds into our last result, which is the proposal of predictive benchmarking protocols connecting simulations to experiments. Our work paves the way for large-scale algorithmic simulations and performance prediction under hardware-relevant noise conditions informed by realistic device characteristics.

AI.tldr: The paper integrates tensor network methods with quantum autoregressive models to analyze and predict the effects of time-correlated noise on quantum algorithms, specifically examining the quantum Fourier transformation.
AI.motivation: To understand and quantify the impact of time-correlated noise on the performance of quantum algorithms, particularly in larger scales under realistic hardware conditions.
AI.method: The study employs tensor network techniques combined with autoregressive moving average models to simulate and analyze noise effects, focusing on infidelity exponents and spectral features related to noise.
AI.result: The findings demonstrate that infidelity scaling exponents can predict algorithm performance at larger scales based on training data from smaller scales, confirming that temporal correlations significantly impact multi-qubit circuits.
AI.conclusion: The research establishes a workflow for predictive benchmarking that links simulations to experimental results, facilitating large-scale simulations and performance predictions under realistic noise conditions.

title: Fusion of JWST data - Demonstrating practical feasibility
summary: Data fusion is a computational process widely used in Earth observation to generate high-resolution hyperspectral data cubes with two spatial and one spectral dimensions. It merges data from instruments with complementary characteristics: one with low spatial but high spectral resolutions, and another with high spatial but low spectral resolutions. In astronomy, the use of such instrumental combinations is becoming increasingly common, making data fusion a promising approach for enhancing observational data. Until now, however, its application to astronomical data has remained unsuccessful. We present the first successful astronomical data fusion using JWST integral field spectroscopy with NIRSpec and imaging across 29 filters with NIRCam. Applied to observations of the d203-506 protoplanetary disk in Orion and of Titan, our method produces fused hyperspectral cubes with NIRCam spatial and NIRSpec spectral resolutions. These results pave the way for extracting the physical properties from JWST data with unprecedented spatial resolution and showcase the transformative potential of data fusion in astronomy.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a successful methodology for fusing astronomical data from JWST's NIRSpec and NIRCam instruments to enhance hyperspectral data analysis.
AI.motivation: To improve the resolution and utility of astronomical data via data fusion techniques that have been previously unsuccessful in the field.
AI.method: The study integrates low spatial, high spectral data from NIRSpec with high spatial, low spectral data from NIRCam across multiple filters to create high-resolution hyperspectral data cubes.
AI.result: The fused data cubes produced from observations of the d203-506 protoplanetary disk and Titan demonstrate enhanced spatial and spectral resolution compared to previous methods.
AI.conclusion: This approach significantly advances data analysis capabilities in astronomy, facilitating the extraction of detailed physical properties from JWST observations.

title: Resolving diffusion signatures in distant pulsar halos with current and future experiments
summary: Pulsar halos provide a unique probe of cosmic-ray propagation in the vicinity of pulsars and have important implications for our understanding of particle diffusion in the interstellar medium. However, the number of firmly identified pulsar halos remains limited. One of the main challenges is the difficulty in unambiguously confirming halo candidates through precise morphological measurements with current $γ$-ray observations. In this work, we investigate the prospects for identifying pulsar halo candidates through morphological discrimination using simulations of two advanced $γ$-ray experiments: LHAASO-KM2A and the Cherenkov Telescope Array (CTA). Using mock observations with realistic instrumental responses, we assess the ability of each experiment to distinguish diffusion-based halo morphologies from alternative simplified spatial models. Our results show that both increased photon statistics and improved angular resolution significantly enhance the power of morphological discrimination. In particular, CTA benefits from its superior angular resolution, while LHAASO-KM2A gains sensitivity from its large effective area at the highest energies. These results indicate that future $γ$-ray observations have the potential to expand the sample of pulsar halos and provide further insights into cosmic-ray transport around pulsars.

AI.tldr: This study explores the potential of LHAASO-KM2A and CTA experiments to identify pulsar halo candidates through morphological analysis of $γ$-ray data.
AI.motivation: Identifying pulsar halos is crucial for understanding cosmic-ray diffusion in the interstellar medium, yet current observational methods face challenges in confirming candidates.
AI.method: Simulations of morphological discrimination using mock observations from two $γ$-ray experiments: LHAASO-KM2A and CTA, assessing each experiment's ability to distinguish halo morphologies.
AI.result: Both experiments showed that higher photon statistics and better angular resolution improved morphological discrimination; CTA excelled in angular resolution, while LHAASO-KM2A offered sensitivity at high energies.
AI.conclusion: Future $γ$-ray observations from these experiments may significantly enlarge the known pulsar halo population and enhance our understanding of cosmic-ray transport.

title: Muon collider experiments as electron/positron beam sources: case studies of new light-particle searches
summary: At muon colliders, muon decays naturally produce intense electrons and positrons with unique features, namely high energies, high repetition rates, and small intrinsic uncertainties, that are unavailable at existing accelerator facilities. We quantitatively study the feasibility of extracting such particles in two representative future muon collider designs, IMCC and $μ$TRISTAN. Using Monte Carlo simulations with the corresponding design parameters, we study the spatial, angular, and energy distributions of decay electrons and positrons in the curved sections of the collider ring. We find that typical deflections of $0.1-10~\mathrm{mrad}$ can be achieved even for high-energy electrons carrying large energy fractions ($\simeq 0.6 - 1.0$) of the muon beam energy, with the ring bending magnets (or magnets providing an equivalent field) effectively serving as a pre-septum magnet, that partially deflects the beam before the main septum magnet, suggesting that the extraction scheme could be practically feasible. Exploiting the distinct beam properties of IMCC and $μ$TRISTAN, we propose complementary search strategies, missing energy and momentum searches for dark matter at $μ$TRISTAN and visible-decay searches for axion-like particles and light scalars at IMCC, which probe parameter space beyond the reach of current and other proposed experiments.

AI.tldr: This study evaluates the extraction of high-energy electrons and positrons from muon decays at future muon colliders IMCC and μTRISTAN, proposing feasible extraction methods to search for dark matter and axion-like particles.
AI.motivation: To explore the unique particle features generated by muon decays, which are not accessible in existing accelerators, and to evaluate their feasibility in future collider designs.
AI.method: Monte Carlo simulations are utilized to assess particle distributions and extraction methods in the curved sections of collider rings for IMCC and μTRISTAN.
AI.result: Deflections of 0.1-10 mrad for high-energy decay electrons are achievable, indicating practical feasibility of the extraction scheme that uses ring bending magnets as pre-septum magnets.
AI.conclusion: Proposed search strategies at the muon colliders could explore unproven parameter space for dark matter and new particles, enhancing the potential for groundbreaking discoveries.

title: Exploring Nucleon Structure and the Proton Mass Problem through Holographic QCD
summary: Understanding the internal structure of the proton-including the distributions of quarks and gluons and their contributions to proton properties such as mass-remains a central challenge in quantum chromodynamics (QCD). While quark generalized parton distributions (GPDs) have been studied extensively, a unified approach that simultaneously extracts quark parton distribution functions (PDFs), gravitational form factors (GFFs), and gluon GPDs from experimental constraints is still lacking. Moreover, the role of gluons in proton mass generation, particularly through the trace anomaly mechanism, requires deeper theoretical and phenomenological exploration. In this study, we first extract quark GPDs in protons using parameterization method based on the electromagnetic form factors provided by Light-Front Holographic QCD (LFHQCD) from which we derive both quark PDFs and their GFFs. We then extend this approach to model gluon GPDs. Our calculations show consistency with experimental data and lattice QCD results and successfully reproduce soft Pomeron behavior. Furthermore, we investigate near-threshold $J/ψ$ production using gauge/string duality to quantify the contribution of the trace anomaly to the proton mass. Our results demonstrate that the parameterization method provides a consistent framework for describing both quark and gluon structure, bridging GPDs, PDFs, and GFFs. The analysis of $J/ψ$ production confirms that the trace anomaly contributes significantly ($\sim 23\%$) to the proton mass, with the calculated cross-section dependence on momentum transfer $t$ in agreement with experimental observations. This work advances the understanding of proton structure by integrating quark and gluon degrees of freedom and elucidating the origin of proton mass within QCD.

AI.tldr: This study develops a unified method for extracting quark and gluon structures in protons, linking GPDs, PDFs, and GFFs, while investigating the trace anomaly's contribution to proton mass.
AI.motivation: The study addresses the complex internal structure of protons, specifically focusing on quark and gluon interactions and their contributions to proton properties like mass, which are inadequately explored in existing research.
AI.method: A parameterization method based on electromagnetic form factors from Light-Front Holographic QCD is employed to extract quark GPDs, PDFs, and GFFs. This approach is then extended to model gluon GPDs and analyze near-threshold $J/ψ$ production using gauge/string duality.
AI.result: The model shows consistency with experimental data and lattice QCD results, reproducing soft Pomeron behavior, and quantifies the trace anomaly's contribution to proton mass at about 23%.
AI.conclusion: The research presents a robust framework integrating quark and gluon characteristics, enhancing comprehension of proton structure and mass origins in QCD.

title: Examination of classical simulations for Heisenberg-Langevin equations for spin-1/2
summary: A system of spins coupled to a bath is a traditional setup in open quantum systems. Through Heisenberg's equation, the spin dynamics can be modeled by a set of first-order differential equations. Interpreting the terms as colored noise and non-Markovian damping, one can write them as quantummechanical Heisenberg-Langevin (HL) equations. These are notoriously difficult to solve because of the high dimensionality of the Hilbert space. Classical generalized Langevin equations, involving non-Markovian damping and colored noise, are well understood and can be treated numerically with relative ease. Thus, a classical ansatz can be made by substituting quantum expectation values with classical functions.
